name: Attendance Allowance

clauses.text: Claimant must have reached State Pension age.
Claimant must have a physical or mental disability or health condition severe enough to need help with personal care or supervision for safety.
Claimant must have needed that help for at least 6 months.
Claimant must have been in Great Britain for at least 2 of the last 3 years.
Claimant cannot get Attendance Allowance if already receiving Disability Living Allowance, Personal Independence Payment, or Adult Disability Payment.
Attendance Allowance is paid at £76.70 a week (lower rate) or £114.60 a week (higher rate); higher rate applies when help is needed both day and night.
Scheme covers England and Wales; people in Scotland apply for Pension Age Disability Payment instead.

notes: Attendance Allowance is for people over State Pension age who need help with personal care or supervision. It has two rates: lower (£76.70/week) if help needed either day or night, higher (£114.60/week) if help needed both day and night. Cannot be claimed if already receiving DLA, PIP, or Adult Disability Payment. Only available in England and Wales.
